title: Rewrite resilience prompt lab
summary: Working lab doc for an onboarding/regression prompt pack that focuses on rewrite and refactor resilience. Targets are compilation correctness, unit-test preservation, and style/constraint adherence when models rewrite or refactor code. This is meant to produce a lightweight, diverse promptbank for model-onboarding and continuous regression checks.
goals: 1) Create a compact, high-signal prompt pack that reveals regressions in: build/compile success, unit test pass rates, and style constraints. 2) Provide reproducible harness commands and metric definitions. 3) Prioritize cases that expose semantic drift (silent functional changes) and brittle unit-test hallucinations.
scope: This pack covers small-to-medium sized python and typescript snippets (5-120 LOC) with focused refactor tasks: rename/reshape, extract-function, loop-to-comprehension, iterative-to-recursive and vice versa, type annotation insertion, and API-adapter style rewrites. Not in scope: large-scale architecture changes, dataset-level transformations, or model-edit style prompts.
prompt_samples:
Prompt A - Preserve tests: 
Input: (original file) calculator.py with functions add(a,b), multiply(a,b) and a tests/test_calculator.py with 12 asserts.
Instruction: Refactor calculator.py to improve clarity and reduce duplication. Do NOT change public behavior demonstrated by tests; update code only, keep function signatures the same. Return only the modified file content.
Prompt B - Insert type hints + lint: 
Input: (original) utils.ts with several any types and tslint complaint lines.
Instruction: Add TypeScript type annotations, remove tslint errors, and ensure build (tsc) passes. Keep the existing exported API stable. Return updated file(s).
Prompt C - Replace recursion with iteration: 
Input: naive fibonacci recursive implementation and tests.
Instruction: Convert recursive fibonacci to an iterative implementation that preserves numeric results for inputs 0..30 and keeps tests passing. Mention any algorithmic complexity differences in a one-line comment. Return code only.
Prompt D - Style constraint enforcement: 
Input: Python module with 120 char lines, missing type hints, and mixed quote styles.
Instruction: Reformat to comply with Black (88 char), add simple type hints where obvious, and normalize to single quotes. Do not change runtime behavior. Return modified file.
Prompt E - Minimal API adapter: 
Input: small microservice handler that uses legacy client.get(path) and tests assume JSON keys.
Instruction: Replace legacy client with new_client.fetch(path, opts) while keeping behavior identical. Include an adapter wrapper and update imports accordingly. Ensure tests still pass.
test_cases: Compilation check: run tsc or python -m py_compile on changed files. Expect 0 stderr exit and no syntax errors.
Unit test validation: run pytest or jest for the changed module's test file(s). Record pass/fail and flakiness across 5 repeated runs.
Behavioral equivalence: golden-input set evaluation (5 example inputs per function) comparing numeric or JSON outputs between original and refactor to detect silent semantic changes.
Style/lint checks: run black --check, flake8, and eslint --max-warnings=0. Record style score and violations.
Performance microbench: optional benchmark for functions where algorithmic complexity could change (e.g., fibonacci). Capture median time for N chosen inputs.
Determinism test: repeat generation with 5 seeds/temperature settings to see whether model sometimes introduces breaking changes.
Edge-condition tests: include null/None, empty collection, and max-length inputs used by existing unit-tests.
metrics_and_thresholds:
- compile_success_rate: target >= 98% across the pack.
- unit_test_pass_rate: target >= 95% (single-run), mean over 5 runs >= 98%.
- semantic_equivalence_score: >= 0.98 on golden-input comparisons (exact match for outputs where deterministic).
- style_conformance: 0 ESLint/Flake8/Black errors for 'style-strict' subset; soft threshold allowed for 'style-loose' subset.
- flaky_change_rate: fraction of prompts that pass only intermittently across repeated runs; target < 2%.
Metrics are computed per-model and per-prompt, stored as CSV rows with fields: prompt_id, model, seed, compile_ok (0/1), tests_passed_count, style_violations_count, semantic_mismatches_count, run_timestamp.
runbook:
Local harness (dev): docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/work ghcr.io/redwood-inference/eval-harness:2026-02 /bin/sh -c 'python -m eval_runner --pack rewrite-resilience --model <MODEL> --out results.csv'
CI: job 'applied-ml/rewrite-resilience' runs on PRs touching applied-ml or model-onboard changes. Use eval-harness tag v2.1. Save artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/rewrite-resilience/<run-id>/
Notes: harness will check out original source snapshots from git commit referenced in prompt metadata. Use TEST_SEED to reproduce flaky failures.
Required infra: ephemeral GPUs for LLM model runs, a small headless Node/Python runtime to run compilers and tests, and an isolated sandbox to execute generated code (time-limited: 15s per test-case).
regression_strategy:
- Weekly scheduled regression on candidate models: run pack against last-known-good model and compare CSV metrics.
- Alert if unit_test_pass_rate drops by >3 percentage points or compile_success_rate drops by >2 percentage points.
- Auto-bisect: run older model checkpoints (if available) to bracket the regression.
- On alert: tag failing prompts as high-priority tickets in ENG-4127 and assign to oncall applied-ml engineer.
- For silent semantic drift: triage includes diff of golden-input outputs and human review of mismatches to determine whether tests were too permissive.
initial_findings:
Smoke run 2026-02-16 against model 'redwood-alpha-v0' produced: compile_success_rate 96.7% (7/210 failures mainly in TypeScript packs due to missing lib DOM types), unit_test_pass_rate 94.2% (flaky_count 3 prompts), semantic_equivalence_score 0.975. Observed common failure modes: truncated file outputs (model omitted import), renaming public API, and inserting new helper functions that change closure behavior.
Action items: add explicit prompt constraints that require listing changed files and include an enforced preamble 'DO NOT change external APIs' and add a small post-check step parsing exports to ensure exported names remain constant.
